Hops 1-4 behave as documented for the runs they get. (b) The hop javadocs match their code; hop 4 says it finds the runs first and then adds each run's nodes, which puts the selection decision in the gold. (c) No competing repair. Padding the list with a null sentinel in hop 3 (also possible in hop 4) passes the trigger, the ownership tests and the full suite, but it only steers the input so the defect is never hit; runsOfType still violates its contract for any list that ends in a run, and nothing in hop 3's docs calls for a sentinel, so this is a masking bypass. A tail re-scan in hop 4 re-tests node types, a second implementation of the gold's decision, so it is a bypass. (d) No leakage. The names are neutral and the gates G2a/G2b are clean. The lie ('The data nodes are counted first, so that the list is created with exactly the capacity it needs.') is procedural and false, and it does not name the omitted run flush. The gold javadoc is silent on the end-of-list run. (e) The gold is exactly five calls below the facade. The hops sit in the five hosts_hop_order files, in order (HttpConnection 706, Evaluator 701 [nested public static CssNthEvaluator at the seeded anchor], Node 667, Elements 561, Whitelist 464), five distinct existing classes in the largest5 regime with Element.java excluded. The facade body is a single delegating call (the original had no guard), and the trigger is an existing test, empty test.patch. correct.patch differs from the variant only by the restored line. (g) C10i rules: dataNodes keeps its signature, modifiers and throws. It is V1 state-as-parameters (it reads the childNodes field), widens no visibility and adds no type, reflection or test edit; it is an allowed candidate with facade_planned_by=null. (f) The convention (every child of the type is selected, the last one included) is pinned outside the gold by the intact sibling filters Element.textNodes and Element.children and by the passing tests testGetTextNodes (' Four' last), testWithSupplementaryCharacter and testManipulateTextNodes.
